AI.tldr: The paper develops a sparse linear solver for computing derivatives of 2D tensor networks implicitly, resolving the open problem of finite entanglement scaling perturbations in critical systems and showing they differ from conformal field theory predictions, while also providing a stable alternative to automatic differentiation for variational optimization of projected entangled pair states.
AI.motivation: To resolve the open problem of determining the actual perturbations induced by matrix product state approximations of critical systems, which were previously assumed to follow conformal field theory predictions.
AI.method: Development of a sparse linear solver that computes forward and backward derivatives of 2D tensor networks implicitly with respect to their defining parameters.
AI.result: The perturbations induced by matrix product state approximations of critical systems are quite different than those predicted by conformal field theory.
AI.conclusion: The proposed implicit differentiation method provides a primitive for variational optimization of projected entangled pair states that circumvents instabilities of traditional automatic differentiation methods.

title: Periodic orbits and quantum many-body scars in integrable spin chains
summary: Quantum many-body scars provide an exception to generic thermalising dynamics, but their relation to integrability remains unclear. Here we apply the periodic-orbit framework to the integrable XYZ/XXZ spin-1/2 chain, developing an energy-resolved approach that enables us to locate and track periodic orbits across the spectrum. We identify families of scarred orbits and resolve their supporting eigenstates in terms of Bethe-ansatz quantum numbers, revealing a common string core dressed by zero-momentum magnon pairs. This allows us to reconstruct both the scarred eigenstates and the associated towers directly within the Bethe ansatz, and explain the equidistant tower spacing analytically from the decoupling of zero-momentum magnon pairs in the Bethe equations, providing a microscopic realisation of scar phenomenology in an integrable setting. We further show that this structure persists upon breaking integrability with a transverse field, with the periodic orbits continuing to govern the dynamics. Our results establish a direct connection between the periodic-orbit picture of quantum scarring and the algebraic structure of integrable models, showing that key features of scar dynamics can be understood analytically within the Bethe ansatz framework.

AI.tldr: The paper uses a periodic-orbit framework in an integrable XYZ/XXZ spin chain to identify quantum many-body scars, reconstruct scarred eigenstates via Bethe ansatz, and show that scar phenomenology persists under weak integrability-breaking perturbations.
AI.motivation: To resolve the unclear relationship between quantum many-body scars and integrability, and to develop an analytic understanding of scar dynamics within an integrable setting.
AI.method: The authors apply the periodic-orbit framework to the integrable XYZ/XXZ spin-1/2 chain, using an energy-resolved approach to locate and track periodic orbits. Scarred eigenstates are identified via Bethe-ansatz quantum numbers, revealing a common string core dressed by zero-momentum magnon pairs. The equidistant tower spacing is explained analytically from decoupling of zero-momentum magnon pairs in the Bethe equations.
AI.result: Families of scarred periodic orbits are identified; scarred eigenstates and their towers are reconstructed within Bethe ansatz; the equidistant level spacing is derived analytically. The structure persists upon breaking integrability with a transverse field.
AI.conclusion: A direct connection is established between the periodic-orbit picture of quantum scarring and the algebraic structure of integrable models, showing that key scar features can be understood analytically within the Bethe ansatz framework.

title: Superadditivity for Entanglement-Assisted Communication
summary: The entanglement-assisted capacity of a quantum channel admits an additive single-letter characterization, implying that joint encodings across channel uses cannot increase the ultimate communication rate. Here, we show that this additive picture does not extend to communication reliability. Specifically, we prove that the Petz-Rényi channel information can be strictly superadditive for every $α\in[1/2,1)$, yielding a genuine multi-copy enhancement of the entanglement-assisted random-coding error exponent, even though the entanglement-assisted capacity remains additive. We establish this phenomenon analytically already for measurement channels, which are entanglement-breaking and have additive unassisted capacity. Remarkably, this strict superadditivity is witnessed by a separable, classically correlated two-copy channel-input marginal, demonstrating that no entanglement between the transmitted systems is required. Our results show that, although correlations across channel uses cannot increase the ultimate rate of entanglement-assisted communication, they can enhance its reliability.

AI.tldr: The entanglement-assisted capacity is additive, but the Petz-Rényi channel information shows strict superadditivity for α∈[1/2,1), meaning multi-copy encoding enhances communication reliability even though the rate limit remains unchanged. This is shown analytically for measurement channels with separable inputs.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that while entanglement-assisted capacity is additive (no rate gain from joint encoding), the reliability (error exponent) can be strictly superadditive, overturning the assumption that additivity extends to all performance metrics.
AI.method: Analytical proof of strict superadditivity of Petz-Rényi channel information for α∈[1/2,1), using measurement channels (entanglement-breaking, additive unassisted capacity) as a testbed, with separable, classically correlated two-copy inputs.
AI.result: Strict superadditivity of the Petz-Rényi channel information is proven for all α∈[1/2,1), yielding a genuine multi-copy enhancement of the entanglement-assisted random-coding error exponent, even though capacity remains additive.
AI.conclusion: Correlations across channel uses cannot increase the entanglement-assisted communication rate but can enhance its reliability, and this effect does not require entanglement between transmitted systems.

title: LDGM-Based Quantum Codes for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
summary: We construct a new family of Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes using the generator and parity-check matrices of Low-Density Generator Matrix (LDGM) codes, with row operations applied to both matrices in order to achieve the desired quantum rate. Decoding is performed in an iterative manner, by applying message passing over the associated graph, and discrete Density Evolution (DDE) is used to optimize performance in the depolarizing channel. The proposed construction offers high flexibility and easiness in the design, producing quantum codes that possess excellent error correction capabilities. By properly designing the structure of the code, we are able to control and bound the weight of the stabilizer generators to a small value, which results in codes particularly well suited for fault-tolerant quantum computation. At the same time, these codes achieve very good performance in terms of error correction capability.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new family of CSS codes built from LDGM codes, using row operations to achieve target quantum rates. Iterative message-passing decoding and discrete density evolution optimization are employed, yielding codes with low-weight stabilizer generators and strong error correction for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
AI.motivation: To construct high-performance quantum CSS codes that are flexible, easy to design, and suitable for fault-tolerant quantum computation, while overcoming limitations of existing quantum code constructions.
AI.method: CSS codes are constructed from LDGM codes by applying row operations to generator and parity-check matrices. Decoding uses iterative message passing over the associated graph, and discrete density evolution (DDE) is employed to optimize performance in the depolarizing channel. The stabilizer generator weights are controlled and bounded through careful code structure design.
AI.result: The proposed codes exhibit high design flexibility, low-weight stabilizer generators, and excellent error correction capability in the depolarizing channel.
AI.conclusion: The LDGM-based CSS code family is well suited for fault-tolerant quantum computation due to its low stabilizer weight and strong error correction, while maintaining ease of design and flexibility.

title: Parameter-Shift Rules for Gradients in Boson Sampling Experiments
summary: Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive $n-$th order parameter-shift rules for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where $n$ photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that in general it is not possible to generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling. Only in the specific case where the transmission matrix of the interferometer can be factorized as a diagonal loss matrix premultiplied by a pure unitary it is possible to obtain parameter-shift rules with a finite order given by twice the total number of photons detected. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method by comparing its performance against finite differences on real hardware.

AI.tldr: The paper derives nth-order parameter-shift rules for computing gradients in lossy Fock boson sampling, shows general impossibility for Gaussian boson sampling except under specific factorization conditions, and validates the method against finite differences on real hardware.
AI.motivation: To enable gradient computation in photonic quantum experiments with loss, specifically for boson sampling transition probabilities, which is needed for variational quantum algorithms and optimization in quantum optics.
AI.method: Derives nth-order parameter-shift rules using a robust photon loss model for Fock boson sampling; analyzes the conditions for extending to Gaussian boson sampling; tests against finite differences on real quantum hardware.
AI.result: nth-order parameter-shift rules work for lossy Fock boson sampling; cannot generalize to Gaussian boson sampling except when the transmission matrix factorizes as diagonal loss premultiplied by a pure unitary, where the shift order is twice the number of detected photons.
AI.conclusion: Parameter-shift rules are viable for gradient computation in lossy Fock boson sampling but have limited applicability to Gaussian boson sampling; the proposed method outperforms finite differences on hardware.

title: Backpropagating Pauli Propagation
summary: We develop a backpropagation algorithm for evaluating parameter gradients in quantum circuits using Pauli propagation simulation. The method has computational complexity comparable to that of standard sparse Pauli simulation techniques, while producing gradients whose accuracy is of the same order as the corresponding observable expectation values. By exploiting the reversibility of quantum circuits, the algorithm reduces the memory cost by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(n_\text{param})$ compared with conventional reverse-mode automatic differentiation, where $n_\text{param}$ denotes the number of parameters in the circuit. Compared with finite difference methods, the algorithm is $\mathcal{O}(n_\text{param})$ more efficient in function evaluations. These features enable efficient and accurate classical optimization of quantum circuits for applications such as state preparation and time-evolution compression, while also allowing operator-complexity measures such as the operator stabilizer Rényi entropy to be monitored and regularized during optimization. We demonstrate the method by optimizing low-energy state-preparation circuits for transverse-field Ising models in one, two, and three dimensions and for the three-dimensional Heisenberg model, and by compressing two-dimensional time-evolution circuits.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a backpropagation algorithm for quantum circuit parameter gradients using Pauli propagation, achieving computational parity with sparse Pauli simulation but with reduced memory cost (factor of O(n_param)) and improved efficiency over finite difference methods (O(n_param) fewer function evaluations). It enables efficient classical optimization of quantum circuits, demonstrated on state preparation and time-evolution compression for various spin models.
AI.motivation: To develop a more efficient method for computing parameter gradients in quantum circuits during classical optimization, addressing memory and computation bottlenecks in existing approaches like reverse-mode automatic differentiation and finite difference methods.
AI.method: A backpropagation algorithm that evaluates parameter gradients via Pauli propagation simulation, leveraging quantum circuit reversibility to reduce memory cost by O(n_param) compared to reverse-mode autodiff, and O(n_param) more efficient in function evaluations than finite difference methods.
AI.result: The method achieves gradient accuracy comparable to observable expectation values, with computational complexity similar to standard sparse Pauli simulation. Demonstrated on optimizing low-energy state-preparation circuits for transverse-field Ising models (1D, 2D, 3D) and the 3D Heisenberg model, and compressing 2D time-evolution circuits.
AI.conclusion: The proposed backpropagation algorithm enables efficient and accurate classical optimization of quantum circuits, while allowing monitoring of operator-complexity measures like operator stabilizer Rényi entropy during optimization, making it suitable for state preparation and time-evolution compression tasks.

title: Entanglement Detection for Two-Qubit and Three-Qubit Pure States via Unitary Transformations and Ancilla State Measurements
summary: Quantum entanglement is the fundamental hallmark of quantum mechanics and a core resource for realizing long-distance quantum communication and scalable linear quantum computing. Accordingly, the precise detection and quantitative quantification of entanglement constitute a foundational and critical problem in quantum information theory. To date, researchers have proposed numerous sufficient conditions for entanglement detection as well as a variety of entanglement measures to characterize the entanglement strength of quantum states; nevertheless, efficient and direct measurement schemes for core entanglement parameters remain underdeveloped. Based on unitary transformations and auxiliary measurements, this paper proposes a set of quantum circuit schemes capable of directly measuring the bipartite concurrence and the tripartite 3-tangle entanglement measure. By introducing auxiliary qubits and constructing specific controlled unitary operations, the proposed scheme maps the analytical expressions of the two entanglement measures onto the measurement probabilities of output states from quantum circuits. It enables efficient and direct quantitative measurement of bipartite and tripartite entanglement without performing full quantum state tomography. This work provides a feasible technical route for the experimental characterization of entanglement properties and lays a groundwork for the practical deployment of multipartite entanglement resources in quantum information processing.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes quantum circuit schemes using unitary transformations and auxiliary measurements to directly measure bipartite concurrence and tripartite 3-tangle entanglement without full state tomography.
AI.motivation: Precise detection and quantitative quantification of entanglement is a foundational problem in quantum information theory, but efficient and direct measurement schemes for core entanglement parameters remain underdeveloped.
AI.method: The method introduces auxiliary qubits and constructs specific controlled unitary operations, mapping the analytical expressions of concurrence and 3-tangle onto measurement probabilities of output states from quantum circuits.
AI.result: The proposed scheme enables efficient and direct quantitative measurement of bipartite and tripartite entanglement without performing full quantum state tomography.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a feasible technical route for experimental characterization of entanglement properties and lays groundwork for practical deployment of multipartite entanglement resources in quantum information processing.

title: Counterexamples to additivity of minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy of quantum channels for $p>3/4$ and $0\leq p<1/4$
summary: Additivity of minimum output entropies is a central problem in quantum information theory. Nonadditivity is known for every Rényi order $p>1$, at the von Neumann point $p=1$, and near $p=0$, while most of the interval $0<p<1$ has remained open. We prove that for every Rényi order $p$ satisfying either $p>3/4$ or $0\leq p<1/4$, there exist finite-dimensional projection-induced quantum channels such that additivity of the minimum output $p$-Rényi entropy fails. The proof combines two correlated random-projection constructions: a product-conjugate Bell-state witness for $p>3/4$, and a transpose-complement rank-defect witness for $p<1/4$. Thus the unresolved part of $0<p<1$ is reduced to $[1/4,3/4]$. Our estimates also improve the output dimension threshold for additivity violation of minimum output von Neumann entropy, first established in Belinschi, Collins and Nechida.

AI.tldr: This paper proves nonadditivity of minimum output Rényi entropy for all p>3/4 and 0≤p<1/4, reducing the unresolved interval to [1/4,3/4], using two random-projection constructions.
AI.motivation: Additivity of minimum output entropies is a central problem in quantum information theory, but while nonadditivity was known for many Rényi orders, most of the interval 0<p<1 remained unresolved.
AI.method: Two correlated random-projection constructions: (1) a product-conjugate Bell-state witness for p>3/4, and (2) a transpose-complement rank-defect witness for p<1/4.
AI.result: Nonadditivity is proven for p>3/4 and 0≤p<1/4, reducing the open interval to [1/4,3/4]; also improves the output dimension threshold for von Neumann entropy violation.
AI.conclusion: The unresolved portion of 0<p<1 is reduced to the interval [1/4,3/4], and the output dimension threshold for additivity violation of minimum output von Neumann entropy is improved.

title: Coulomb blockade in microscopic material defects as a source of decoherence and noise in solid-state quantum circuits
summary: A critical limitation of solid-state quantum devices arises from the materials from which they are fabricated: uncontrolled surfaces, interfaces, and structural imperfections introduce numerous sources of loss and decoherence. Despite extensive efforts, linking these decoherence mechanisms to their microscopic material origins -- essential for developing effective mitigation strategies -- remains an outstanding challenge that has slowed coherence improvements. Here, using scanning gate microscopy on live superconducting circuits we identify a previously unrecognised decoherence mechanism originating from Coulomb blockade and microwave-driven charge tunnelling in metallic grains. Such grains are ubiquitous in thin-film devices fabricated by standard lithography processes. By characterising multiple defects across different devices, we find such defects to be as common and as debilitating to device performance as two-level system (TLS) defects, while originating from a fundamentally different physical mechanism. Importantly, conventional characterisation techniques would misattribute this loss to other, microwave power-independent processes. Our observations thus reveal a widespread source of decoherence in superconducting circuits, challenging the prevailing paradigm that coherence lifetimes are primarily limited by TLS defects. Eliminating metallic grains during fabrication provides a clear and practical route to suppress this mechanism, offering a pathway towards improved coherence and reduced noise in microwave-based solid-state quantum devices.

AI.tldr: Metallic grains in thin-film superconducting devices cause decoherence via Coulomb blockade and charge tunnelling, a mechanism as prevalent as TLS defects but distinct, often misidentified, and mitigable by eliminating grains during fabrication.
AI.motivation: Solid-state quantum devices suffer from decoherence due to uncontrolled surfaces, interfaces, and imperfections, but linking decoherence to specific microscopic material origins has remained a major challenge hindering coherence improvements.
AI.method: Scanning gate microscopy performed on live superconducting circuits to identify and characterize decoherence mechanisms at the microscopic scale across multiple devices.
AI.result: Discovered that Coulomb blockade and microwave-driven charge tunnelling in ubiquitous metallic grains cause decoherence as common and debilitating as TLS defects, but conventional techniques misattribute this loss to power-independent processes.
AI.conclusion: Metallic grains represent a widespread, previously unrecognized decoherence source challenging the TLS-centric paradigm; eliminating them during fabrication offers a practical route to improved coherence and reduced noise in microwave-based solid-state quantum devices.

title: Dynamic Entanglement Distribution for Multi-User and Multi-Protocol Quantum Networking
summary: Dynamic entanglement distribution is a key requirement for scalable, multi-user and multi-protocol quantum networks. We demonstrate a metropolitan-scale entanglement-based quantum communication network enabled by a quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM), which dynamically distributes polarisation-entangled photon pairs from a broadband source to six users over deployed campus and metropolitan fibre. The network supports programmable full-mesh, partial-mesh and sliced sub-network configurations, enabling flexible allocation of entanglement resources according to link condition and service requirement. We demonstrate stable six-user full-mesh operation over more than 150 hours, compare full-mesh and time-shared partial-mesh strategies under different source and detector conditions, and realise quantum network slicing with optional/additional interconnection links. We also show that the same infrastructure can support different quantum protocols by showcasing Secure Inaugural Authentication-Transfer (SIAT) combined with Network flooding over multiple paths to improve the security of onboarding a new user. These results demonstrate a q-ROADM-enabled entanglement distribution architecture as a novel route towards reconfigurable, service-oriented quantum networking over optical fibre infrastructure.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates a metropolitan-scale entanglement-based quantum communication network using a quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM) that dynamically distributes polarization-entangled photon pairs to six users over deployed fiber, supporting flexible network configurations, stable long-term operation, and multiple quantum protocols.
AI.motivation: Dynamic entanglement distribution is a key requirement for scalable, multi-user and multi-protocol quantum networks, motivating the need for reconfigurable architectures that can flexibly allocate entanglement resources.
AI.method: A quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM) dynamically distributes polarization-entangled photon pairs from a broadband source to six users over deployed campus and metropolitan fiber, supporting programmable full-mesh, partial-mesh, and sliced sub-network configurations.
AI.result: Stable six-user full-mesh operation over more than 150 hours; comparison of full-mesh and time-shared partial-mesh strategies under different source/detector conditions; demonstration of quantum network slicing with interconnection links; and support for Secure Inaugural Authentication-Transfer (SIAT) combined with Network flooding over multiple paths to improve user onboarding security.
AI.conclusion: The q-ROADM-enabled entanglement distribution architecture represents a novel route towards reconfigurable, service-oriented quantum networking over optical fiber infrastructure.
